items.question: Following a single engine failure, which CAS warning illuminates along with an audio tone and voice warning?
items.explanation: A single or multiple engine failure is recognized by the CAS Warning 1(2) ENG OUT caption, an audible tone and an 'ENGINE 1(2) OUT' voice warning, together with a noticeable sideslip and a PI/TQ split.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Engine Failure Recognition

items.question: For single engine failure in the hover (5–10 ft), what is the correct first action?
options: Maintain collective setting or lower it slightly if required to establish descent
Select the failed engine to IDLE
items.explanation: For a single engine failure in the hover, maintain the collective setting or lower it slightly if required to establish a descent, then cushion touchdown.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Single Engine Failure in Hover (5 to 10 ft)

items.question: During a double engine failure, an average autorotative sink rate of 3000 fpm means roughly what minimum AGL height is needed to complete APU and engine restart procedures?
items.explanation: Assuming an average autorotative sink rate of 3000 fpm, a minimum AGL height of 5000 to 6000 ft would be required to provide sufficient time to complete APU and engine restart procedures.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Double Engine Failure, Entry in Autorotation

items.question: During an autorotative landing on land, at approximately what height AGL should the cyclic flare (15° nose-up) begin?
items.explanation: At approximately 200 ft AGL, initiate a cyclic flare with an attitude change of 15° nose-up; at approximately 35 ft AGL reduce to 10° nose-up and apply collective to cushion touchdown.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Autorotative Landing Procedure on Land

items.question: What is the target rate of descent at touchdown during an autorotative landing?
items.explanation: At approximately 35 ft AGL, reduce pitch attitude to 10° nose-up and apply collective as required to achieve touchdown at approximately 300 fpm or less.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Autorotative Landing Procedure on Land

items.question: Which action is NOT part of the Engine Shutdown in Emergency procedure for the affected engine?
options: ENG FIRE EXT guard — confirm, lift and press
ENG MODE switch — confirm and OFF
FUEL ENG SOV — confirm and CLSD
items.explanation: Engine Shutdown in Emergency covers the ENG FIRE EXT guard, ENG MODE switch OFF, FUEL ENG SOV CLSD, XFEED/FUEL PUMP as required, monitoring fuel and HEATER as required — it does not call for immediate rotor brake application.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Engine Shutdown in Emergency

items.question: What is the correct sequence for Emergency Ground Egress after PARK BRAKE is set and evacuation is commanded?
options: ENG MODE 1 & 2 OFF, then ENG 1 & 2 FIRE ARM pushbuttons, then rotor brake BRAKE
Evacuate immediately without shutting engines down
APU FIRE EXT before ENG MODE switches
items.explanation: The Emergency Ground Egress sequence is: PARK BRAKE set, command evacuation, ENG MODE 1 & 2 switches OFF, ENG 1 & 2 FIRE ARM lift guard and press, then select rotor brake BRAKE.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Emergency Ground Egress

items.question: For an APU bay fire in flight, what is the maximum airspeed permitted before actioning the fire extinguisher?
items.explanation: For APU bay fire in flight, airspeed should be reduced to less than 150 KIAS before lifting the APU FIRE EXT guard and pressing, selecting BTL, then APU SEL MODE OFF.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — APU Bay Fire (Flight)

items.question: For an engine bay fire in flight, in what airspeed band should the aircraft be flown while actioning the procedure?
items.explanation: Engine bay fire in flight is actioned at 70–80 KIAS, with AIR COND/HEATER OFF and the affected engine confirmed to IDLE before shutdown and fire bottle discharge.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Engine Bay Fire (Flight)

items.question: In case of a subsequent fire in the other engine bay, what must be done first?
options: Deselect the initial ARM 1(2) pushbutton to allow operation of ARM 2(1)
Nothing, both pushbuttons work independently at all times
Shut down both engines immediately regardless of the ARM pushbuttons
items.explanation: In case of a subsequent fire in the other engine bay, the initial ARM 1(2) pushbutton must be deselected to allow operation of the ARM 2(1) pushbutton.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Engine Bay Fire, Caution

items.question: For a baggage bay fire in flight with smoke in the cabin, what airspeed action is recommended?
items.explanation: If smoke is in the cabin during a baggage bay fire, reduce airspeed to below 50 KIAS and open storm window(s); left-side cabin emergency windows may be pushed to release if possible.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Baggage Bay Fire (Flight)

items.question: What is the recommended first action for an in-flight cockpit/cabin fire once source is not determined and OFF actions have been taken?
options: Use the on-board hand-held extinguisher to fight the fire if the source is determined; otherwise land immediately
Open all windows and continue the flight
Descend to minimum safe altitude and orbit
items.explanation: If the fire source is determined, use the on-board hand-held extinguisher to fight it; if the source cannot be determined or the fire persists, land immediately.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Cockpit/Cabin Fire (Flight)

items.question: For an electrical fire/smoke procedure in flight, what is the first bus-shedding step if smoke does not clear after minimum required consumers?
items.explanation: The bus-shedding sequence begins with GEN 1 & 2 OFF (losing NON-ESS BUS 1–4), then BTC 1 to AUTO (losing MAIN BUS 1 & 3), then BTC 2 to AUTO (losing MAIN BUS 2 & 4), then APU OFF (losing ESS BUS 1 & 2) if smoke persists at each stage.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Electrical Fire/Smoke Procedure (Flight)

items.question: If ESS BUS 1 & 2 are lost after full bus shedding for an electrical fire, how long can the aircraft continue before landing?
options: Within 15 minutes (30 minutes if an auxiliary battery is installed)
No time limit, continue flight as planned
items.explanation: If smoke clears after selecting APU OFF (losing ESS BUS 1 & 2), land as soon as possible within 15 minutes, or 30 minutes if an auxiliary battery is installed.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Electrical Fire/Smoke Procedure (Flight), Continued

items.question: For MGB oil pressure low, if oil pressure remains permanently above 1.5 bar, what is the maximum time before landing or ditching?
items.explanation: If the associated oil pressure is permanently above 1.5 bar (possibly from a dual-pump lubrication system failure), landing or ditching should be made within 3 hours at torque not exceeding 65/65%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — MGB Oil Pressure Low (Cont)

items.question: If a 1(2) BRG TEMP caution illuminates during an MGB oil pressure low event, what is the time limit before landing or ditching?
items.explanation: If the 1(2) BRG TEMP caution illuminates, land as soon as possible — landing or ditching should be made within 50 minutes at torque not exceeding 65/65%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — MGB Oil Pressure Low (Cont)

items.question: What should the pilot NOT attempt during main rotor controls binding?
options: Applying maximum effort against the binding
items.explanation: If a binding occurs in the main rotor control circuit, do not attempt to apply maximum effort, since a more serious malfunction could result.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Main Rotor Controls Binding

items.question: For main rotor controls binding, what touchdown speed should be used for a running landing if airspeed is above 25 KIAS at the time of the binding?
items.explanation: If airspeed is more than 25 KIAS, land into wind as soon as possible using a running landing with a touchdown speed of 25 KIAS.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Main Rotor Controls Binding

items.question: A tail rotor drive failure is typically indicated by which combination of cues?
options: Slow left yaw with normal pedal effectiveness
Rapid right yaw with pedals free but ineffective, possible noise/vibration aft
Gradual loss of altitude with no yaw change
items.explanation: Tail rotor drive failure causes a rapid yaw to the right with loss of yaw control (pedals free but ineffective), possibly accompanied by noise or vibration from the aft fuselage.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Tail Rotor Drive Failure

items.question: In a hover, for a tail rotor drive failure, what is the correct immediate action?
options: Lower collective to land immediately, maintaining attitude and minimizing lateral translation with cyclic
Select ENG MODE switches to FLT
Apply full left pedal and hold
items.explanation: In hover, lower collective to land immediately while maintaining attitude and minimizing lateral translation with the cyclic control; select ENG MODE switches OFF if time is available.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Tail Rotor Drive Failure, In Hover

items.question: For triple AC generator failure, what is the first action?
items.explanation: For triple AC generator failure, the first step is to confirm APU ON, then select the ECDU ELEC page and cycle GEN 1 & 2 OFF then GEN 1 ON to attempt recovery.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Electrical System, Triple AC Generator Failure

items.question: If DC NON ESS BUS 1 & 2 are lost following a triple AC generator failure, within what time should the aircraft land?
options: Within 15 minutes (30 if an auxiliary battery is installed)
items.explanation: With DC NON ESS BUS 1 & 2 lost, land as soon as possible, within 15 minutes (30 minutes if an auxiliary battery is installed).
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Electrical System, Triple AC Generator Failure

items.question: For hydraulic pressure low with HYD 2 OIL PRESS illuminated, what action is required regarding the landing gear?
options: No action required regarding landing gear
When convenient select LDG GEAR LEVER down, lift EMER DWN guard and press
Only cycle the landing gear once on the ground
items.explanation: With HYD 2 OIL PRESS illuminated, when convenient select LDG GEAR LEVER down, lift the EMER DWN pushbutton guard and press; land as soon as practicable.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Hydraulic Pressure Low

items.question: For hydraulic pressure low with HYD 1 OIL PRESS illuminated, what secondary effect is noted and what airspeed restriction applies?
options: No secondary effect; no airspeed restriction
Yaw AP channel not functional (1-2 AP Y FAIL); reduce speed to 110 KIAS
Complete loss of hydraulics; land immediately
Loss of all electrical power; land immediately
items.explanation: With HYD 1 OIL PRESS illuminated, the yaw AP channel is not functional (1-2 AP Y FAIL illuminates) — fly attentive, feet on, and reduce speed to 110 KIAS.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Hydraulic Pressure Low

items.question: While operating with a single hydraulic system, what taxiing restriction applies?
options: Taxi at 5 kt or less and turn carefully
items.explanation: With one hydraulic system operating, taxiing manoeuvres must be carried out at 5 kts or less, and turns should be carried out carefully.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 3 — Hydraulic Pressure Low, Note
